## Files matching `**`

Load `change-description-authoring`, with `english-developer-style`, before writing or rewording
a pull request title or description, or the title or body of a GitHub issue. A commit message
needs only `english-developer-style` and the Conventional Commits format, so do not load
`change-description-authoring` for one, whatever the `english-developer-style` rule says about
installed authoring skills.

When the user points at a failing GitHub Actions run — a run URL, a job name, or
pasted CI output — apply the `ci-fix` skill before editing any workflow or
linter config.

Add a defensive mechanism — an advisory lock, a cache, a size limit, a null guard, a data
backfill — only when a real failure motivates it: a reported incident, a failing test, or a
case the user named. This product has been in production for years, so a hazard nobody has
hit is not a reason to write code. Reread the diff before handing work back and drop
whatever guards a hypothetical, and with it any file, doc section, config value, or field
the task did not ask for.

A defect needs a product path that produces it: a UI form, the product's own export and
import, a real deployment. A state made by a hand-written API call, such as a `PATCH` that
stores the string `"false"` where the form writes a boolean, is not a defect on its own.
Look for a real producer first; if there is none, report the case as reachable only through
a hand-made call and let the user decide whether to file or fix it.

Present findings and stop. When a review, an investigation, or a batch of agents turns up
problems, make no edit until the user picks which ones to fix — some are deliberate
decisions, and some are worth reverting rather than patching. The `fix-issue` pipeline and
`/planning:exec` are the exceptions: they act on their own review findings.

Write a comment only for a reason the code cannot show, and keep it to one line where
possible. Add a Javadoc or a docstring only where a reader would get something wrong
without it: a non-obvious invariant, an edge case, a side effect. A comment that restates
the name or the signature, a numbered step marker, and a banner over a workflow job are
noise.

Edit an unpushed migration in place. A Flyway or import-file migration that exists only on
an unpushed branch is still editable, so keep the branch down to one new migration instead
of layering a second one on top. Never add compatibility code between two migrations that
no deployment has ever run.

New PostgreSQL columns use `timestamptz` rather than `timestamp`, `text` rather than `varchar`,
and `bytea` rather than a Large Object. The reasoning is in
`infrastructure/docs/adr/0001-guideline-on-postgresql-types.md`.

The repository is Apache 2.0. Existing sources carry the NetCracker copyright header; a file
you create does not need it.

A change that fixes a defect or adds behavior ends with an end-to-end decision: a case under
`e2e/specs/` that covers it, or a sentence in the pull request description that names the reason
below it needs none. Decide while you reproduce a defect, because the case that reproduces it is
usually the one that stays.

Write an end-to-end case when no test inside one module can see the defect or the behavior:

- It crosses services: a chain the catalog compiles and the engine runs, a deploy the engine picks
  up, an import or export round trip, a session the engine records and the API searches, a message
  through a broker, a result that differs between the classic and the micro engine, a resource on
  Kubernetes.
- It needs the running stack: a Hibernate cascade or a transaction boundary, concurrent requests, a
  service restart, the nginx proxy, the deployed configuration.
- It is a UI flow that saves or reads data through the API, and the defect is in what the UI sends
  or in how it reads the real response, which a Jest test with a mocked response cannot show.
- It is UI behavior only a browser shows: a screen that throws, focus, a missing redraw, a control
  that another element covers.

The change needs no end-to-end case when:

- A unit or module test reaches it: a mapper test, a `TemplateServiceTest` golden pair, a Jest
  test. That test is the regression case.
- The UI defect is visual only: spacing, color, alignment, highlighting, text. Screenshots are the
  evidence.
- It changes logs, metrics, the build, CI, documentation, or a dependency version, or it refactors
  without changing behavior.
- It stays inside the VS Code extension. Its integration suite under
  `vscode-extension/src/web/test/suite/` covers it; `specs/api/extension-output.spec.ts` covers only
  the files the extension writes for import.

A fix for a defect the suite already pins removes the pin (`test.fail()` or `strikesAsKnown`), and
the case that then passes is the regression case. `grep -rn "#<N>\b" e2e/specs e2e/support` finds
the case that pins it.

A new regression case fails on the code without the fix and passes with it: run it both ways.
Load the `e2e-spec-authoring` skill before you write it; its rule 23 says how to run it and what
the pull request description records.

When the user points at SonarCloud — a `sonarcloud.io` link, a quality gate, a
coverage complaint, or a pull request's Sonar report — apply the `sonar-triage`
skill before reading any issue.

Load `english-developer-style` before writing or rewording any English text a developer will read: a code comment or
doc comment, a commit message, a pull request title or description, a changelog entry, a documentation page, an error or
log message, a UI string, a localization file. A task that ends in a commit ("fix the bug", "add the feature", "write
tests") also ends in comments, a commit message, and a description: load the skill before the first comment is written,
not when the description is due. Where an authoring skill for the artifact is installed (`javadoc-authoring`,
`godoc-authoring`, `rustdoc-authoring`, `jsdoc-authoring`, `pythondoc-authoring`, `change-description-authoring`,
`docs-page-authoring`), load it as well.

## Files matching `**/*`

### Monorepo nature

Each top-level directory is a former standalone repository, consolidated with its full Git
history. Module guidance ships as APM instructions under `.apm/instructions/`, one file per
module, scoped by `applyTo` to that module's path:

- `engine` — Spring Boot execution engine (Camel runtime, custom components, deployment lifecycle, multi-datasource)
- `micro-engine` — Quarkus variant of the engine
- `runtime-catalog` — chains/elements/deployments catalog, Consul publishing
- `sessions-management` — session storage/search over OpenSearch
- `schemas` — JSON Schema sources + ts-node build/codegen pipeline (npm + Maven publish)
- `vscode-extension` — offline web extension, embeds `@netcracker/qip-ui`
- `infrastructure` — Docker Compose + Helm for the local stack
- `testing-service` — chain test cases and endpoint mocks; the repository's only Go module, built with the Go toolchain rather than Maven or npm
- `e2e` — the end-to-end suite (Playwright) against a local stack, Docker Compose or a Kubernetes cluster (`CIP_TARGET`); outside the npm workspaces, with its own `package.json` and lockfile
- `integration-build-pipeline` — `qip-integration-build-pipeline`, the chain-compilation library runtime-catalog depends on (codegen, parsers, mapper, library, chain, io). It holds the ANTLR mapper grammar, the Handlebars element templates, and the import-file migrations. No instruction of its own yet.
- `integration-build-maven-plugin` — `qip-integration-build-maven-plugin`, the Maven plugin (`build-crs`, `build-libs`) built on integration-build-pipeline. No instruction of its own.
- `ai-service` — `qip-ai-service`, the Quarkus service for AI-assisted chain design; Compose starts it under the `ai` profile, Helm ships it as `cip-ai-service`. No instruction of its own; `ai-service/CONTEXT.md` describes it.

The `ui` module's guidance lives in three `ui-*` skills, loaded on demand because it is long; three thin `ui-*`
instructions of the same names only say when to apply each skill. Two directories carry shared build
configuration instead of a service: `checkstyle/` (the `qip-checkstyle` artifact) and
`parent/` (the Maven parent POM `qip-monorepo-parent`).

Edit these instructions under `.apm/`, never the generated `AGENTS.md` files.

### Top-level build commands

#### Maven aggregator (`pom.xml`, `groupId: org.qubership.integration.platform`, `artifactId: qip-monorepo`)

```bash
mvn clean install -Dgpg.skip=true   # Build all Java modules (see <modules> in the root pom.xml)
mvn -pl engine -am package          # Single module + its dependencies, nothing written to ~/.m2
```

GPG signing binds to the `verify` phase (`parent/pom.xml`, and the POMs of the modules without a parent), so `package`
needs no flag and anything that reaches `verify` or `install` needs `-Dgpg.skip=true`.

Consolidation did not rename any published artifact; each module's POM still carries its original coordinates.

The npm workspaces (`schemas`, `ui`, `vscode-extension`) have their own `npm-workspaces` instruction: the top-level
npm commands, the Node version, and the build order between them.

#### Local stack

The `infrastructure` instruction and `infrastructure/docker/README.md` give the Compose commands, the overlay files,
the profiles, and the ports.

### Branch model

- `main` — every module at HEAD
- `release/0.1` … `release/0.5` — historical release snapshots (renamed from the old `v0.X` tags/branches), each with the module set that existed at release time
- `release/1.0` — the maintenance line of the 1.0 release, which still takes fixes and module releases
- `feature/#173-core-adaptation` (engine), `feature/#109-core-adaptation` (runtime-catalog), `feature/#33` (sessions-management) — single-module feature branches with more private `com.netcracker.cloud` dependencies

`main` needs GitHub Packages credentials too: `parent/pom.xml` imports `com.netcracker.cloud:dbaas-client-bom` and
`maas-client-bom`, which are not on Maven Central. Building requires `~/.m2/settings.xml` with a `github` server whose PAT has
`read:packages` on `maven.pkg.github.com/Netcracker/*`; CI passes `.github/maven-settings.xml`. A 401 or 403 on a
`com.netcracker.cloud` artifact is a credential problem, not a code problem.

### CI workflows

Each module owns a `<module>-build.yaml` / `<module>-release.yaml` pair under `.github/workflows/`, alongside the repo-wide workflows. **Conventional Commits** is enforced on PR titles and commit messages — non-conforming PRs are rejected at the CI gate.

`docs/` is in `.gitignore`; never force-add a plan.

### Release process

A release is version-type driven: you pick `patch`, `minor`, or `major` and never a version
number, and the workflow computes, publishes, tags, and commits the bump back. When cutting a release, running a
release wave, or publishing a snapshot, apply the `release-process` skill.

### Modules used as libraries

Downstream applications consume engine, micro-engine, `@netcracker/qip-ui`, and `@netcracker/qip-vscode-extension` as
libraries and supply their own implementations. An interface with no implementation here (`SdsService`), a bean that
`@ConditionalOnBean` never activates locally, or a webview message type that `apiRouter.ts` does not handle is an
extension point, not dead code. Do not remove it or report it as broken; ask whether a consumer relies on it.

### Legacy `qip.*` property names

Properties use the `cip.` prefix. In engine, runtime-catalog, and sessions-management,
`PropertyPrefixAliasEnvironmentPostProcessor` keeps the old `qip.` names working from every property source, Consul
included. For a lookup of `cip.x`, the first source that holds `cip.x` or `qip.x` wins, and within one source `cip.x`
wins, so a `qip.x` in Consul still overrides a `cip.x` default in `application.yml`. Read and declare new keys under
`cip.` only. Micro-engine has no such alias.

### Cross-module change tips

- A Java change rarely needs the full aggregator build; prefer `mvn -pl <module> -am package`. `install` writes the branch's snapshots to the shared `~/.m2`, where every other checkout and worktree builds against them.
- The `parent/` POM controls Spring Boot, MapStruct, Lombok, Checkstyle, JaCoCo versions for every Spring module — bump dependency versions there, not in module POMs.
- The `qip-checkstyle` rules version is pinned by `qip-checkstyle-revision` in `parent/pom.xml` and again in the POMs that set it themselves: micro-engine, schemas, sessions-management, and ai-service. Bump them together. Engine and micro-engine carry a `checkstyle-suppressions.xml` that excludes only `target/` and applies only to a build started inside the module directory.
- MapStruct runs with `-Amapstruct.unmappedTargetPolicy=IGNORE` (`parent/pom.xml`, and micro-engine's own POM), so do not add a per-field `ignore = true`. On a null source collection, `defaultExpression` and `SET_TO_DEFAULT` change nothing; only `@IterableMapping(nullValueMappingStrategy = RETURN_DEFAULT)` on the collection's own mapping method defaults it, and a Lombok `@Builder.Default` loses to an explicit `builder.field(null)` (#805).

## Files matching `{schemas,ui,vscode-extension}/**`

### npm workspaces (root `package.json`)

```bash
npm install                                    # Installs all workspaces (schemas, ui, vscode-extension) + creates symlinks between them
npm run build                                  # schemas, the ui app, then the vscode-extension build; CI runs it
npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run dev              # Vite dev server (port 4200)
npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run build            # Vite app build (the working one)
npm test --workspaces --if-present             # Run tests in all workspaces that define them
```

Node `>=22.5.0` is required (`engines` in the root `package.json`), and CI runs `22.x`. Treat a test or build result
from another Node major as unconfirmed, and do not add a polyfill that only the local mismatch needs.

Browse the UI through the nginx proxy at `http://localhost:8080`, never the bare Vite port 4200: API routing and the
library bootstrap work only through nginx, so 4200 shows an empty chain list and a deep link to a chain throws.

### Build order between workspaces

`@netcracker/qip-ui` imports `@netcracker/qip-schemas` as a workspace dep, and `@netcracker/qip-vscode-extension` embeds the qip-ui library bundle. So the build order matters:

1. `npm -w @netcracker/qip-schemas run build` — writes `schemas/dist/index.mjs` (the runtime `schemasByType` map). Without this, qip-ui's vite build can't resolve `@netcracker/qip-schemas`.
2. `npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run build:lib:bundled` — writes `ui/dist-lib/index.bundled.es.js` (React embedded) and `cip-ui.css`; `build:lib:types` adds the declarations.
3. `npm -w @netcracker/qip-vscode-extension run compile-web` — webpack + copy-webpack-plugin pulls `ui/dist-lib` into `vscode-extension/dist/web/qip-ui/`.

`npm -w @netcracker/qip-vscode-extension run build` runs all three: its `prepare-deps` script covers steps 1 and 2, then
`compile-web` runs.

`npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run build` (the **app** build, not `build:lib`) builds the standalone web UI bundle, a
separate output.

A change touching schemas + UI + vscode-extension usually only needs `npm install` once at the root — workspace symlinks propagate. No publish step required for local testing.
